title: Hosted-to-Private Migration: Performance Audit & Consumption Playbook (PRD + Design)
author: Miguel Ortega
body:
Summary:
This document defines a product requirements / design playbook used by Account Engineering, Solutions, and Product to plan and execute customer migrations from Redwood Hosted inference to Redwood Private (VPC or on-prem) with a particular focus on preserving production performance, cost estimates, and SLO compliance. The playbook combines measurable audit steps, a test harness, a staged rollout plan, and remediation paths for common performance regressions.

Goals and success criteria:
- Primary goal: enable customers to migrate to Redwood Private with no more than a 10% regression in P50 latency and maintain >= 99.5% request success rate at pre-migration traffic profile within 30 days of cutover.
- Secondary goals:
  - Provide deterministic steps that allow SRE/Product to validate performance parity before accepting final cutover.
  - Produce an upfront consumption forecast (tokens, GPU-hours) and a delta estimate vs Hosted.
  - Capture a reusable set of telemetry checks and load profiles to compare variant behaviour across hardware and network topologies.

Scope:
- In-scope:
  - Migrations from Redwood Hosted API to Redwood Private (VPC-hosted or customer-managed on-prem package).
  - Workloads using text generation, chat, and embeddings.
  - Validation against production-like traffic sampled via traffic mirroring or recorded traces.
- Out-of-scope:
  - Full re-architecture of customer application code.
  - Model re-training or model-contract changes.

Non-goals:
- Guaranteeing identical absolute latency numbers (network differences exist). The focus is on bounded regressions as defined in success criteria.

Requirements (functional):
1) Migration audit checklist (must-have):
   - Collect production traces (last 7 days) and extract representative traffic slices by route, sequence length, and metadata tags.
   - Produce token distribution histogram, concurrent-request histogram, and top-10 routes by QPS.
   - Verify model variant, quantization profile, and fallback routes used in Hosted.
2) Pre-cutover validation harness (must-have):
   - Deploy a Private test cluster with identical model variant(s), quantization, and batcher configuration.
   - Replay traffic with preserved inter-arrival times and session affinity where possible.
   - Measure: P50/P90/P99 latency, TPS, GPU utilization, KV cache hit rate, and memory pressure.
3) Consumption forecaster (should-have):
   - Export a per-route per-hour token and inference-count forecast for 30/90 day windows.
   - Provide delta estimate vs Hosted pricing model and a recommended Dedicated-equivalent capacity if the customer later converts.
4) Rollback and fallback controls (must-have):
   - Canary percentage knobs, automatic rollback triggers based on latency or error budget burn > 5% in 15 minutes.
   - Fallback routing from Private -> Hosted for all customer routes with transparent observability and billing attribution.

Requirements (non-functional):
- Telemetry latency: diagnostic traces and metrics must be available within 2 minutes after test run completion.
- Test harness reproducibility: a runbook and a configurable harness repository shall produce identical runs given the same trace input.
- Security: migration artifacts may contain customer PII; ensure artifacts are stored in customer-scoped S3 (or customer's storage) and encrypted with KMS.

Design overview:
- Components:
  - Migration Auditor: CLI tool that ingests production traces, partitions by route/tenant, and generates workload summaries (token histograms, sequence-length distributions). Output: migration-manifest.json
  - Private Test Cluster: ephemeral Private deployment configured from migration-manifest.json (model pins, quantization profiles, batcher config).
  - Replay Orchestrator: orchestrates traffic replay, collects metrics, and supports session replay when available.
  - Comparator Dashboard: compares Hosted baseline vs Private test results and highlights regressions and resource anomalies.

Migration artifact example (migration-manifest.json snippet):
- route: "/chat-complete"
- model_variant: "redwood-1.3-quant"
- token_histogram: "buckets: [0-32,33-128,...]"
- desired_concurrency: "20"

Telemetry & observability (detailed checks):
- Latency buckets: P50/P90/P99 measured at route-level and model-variant level. Alert if P90 delta > 20% or P99 delta > 10% depending on baseline SLA.
- KV cache effectiveness: measure prefix/KV cache hit ratio. Alert if hit ratio drops > 15 percentage points from baseline.
- GPU-level metrics: SM utilization, memory utilization, context-switch rate, and observed inference batch sizes.
- Network topology checks: egress/ingress bandwidths and RTTs to model-serving hosts.

Runbook: step-by-step migration (numbered):
1) Initiate migration audit: run Auditor against last 7 days traces, push migration-manifest.json to customer-scoped storage.
2) Provision Private Test Cluster: use migration-manifest to provision ephemeral cluster tagged `migration-{tenant}-{date}`.
3) Baseline capture: capture Hosted baseline by replaying a short canonical subset (5–10 minutes) and persist metrics.
4) Full replay: run full replay for a configurable window (recommended: 2 hours covering 95th percentile traffic).
5) Analyze comparator dashboard: review regressions and resource headroom. Document findings in a migration ticket with clear remediation actions.
6) Remediation & hardening: iterate on batcher config, kernel selection, or model quantization profile if required. Re-run targeted replays to validate.
7) Canary cutover: enable 1% traffic to Private for 30 minutes with automated rollback thresholds (latency or error budget).
8) Gradual ramp: follow exponential ramp (1%, 5%, 15%, 50%, 100%) with at least 30–60 minutes between steps and extended guardrails for critical routes.
9) Post-cutover validation: run 24-hour monitoring, confirm success criteria met, and close migration ticket.
10) Optional: provide customer-facing migration report summarizing consumption delta and recommended Dedicated sizing.

Test cases and acceptance criteria:
- Functional tests:
  - Replay fidelity: given an input trace, the orchestrator must preserve session affinity in >= 80% of replayed flows when session IDs exist.
  - Fallback test: simulate Private node failure and verify automatic routing to Hosted within 30s.
- Performance acceptance:
  - For the production slice run, P50 regression <= 10% and request success rate >= 99.5% OR documented plan with tradeoffs and customer consent.

Pricing & consumption guidance for sales and finance:
- Provide a delta estimate template (CSV) that maps historical Hosted token usage to predicted Private GPU-hours and an estimated monthly cost.
- Flag customers where Private cost > Hosted by 30%+ to trigger a commercial review for Dedicated conversion options.
- Indicate any one-time Professional Services day estimates required for large migrations (> 10 routes or > 1M daily tokens).

Ownership and roles:
- Product (owner): Miguel Ortega — product requirements, playbook iterations.
- Solutions / Account Eng: run migration audit and customer coordination.
- SRE: provide test cluster provisioning and ramp controls.
- Customer Success: communicate runbook and obtain business approvals.

Timeline and milestones (recommended cadence):
- Week 0: Audit + migration-manifest generation.
- Week 1: Provision test cluster + baseline replay.
- Week 2: Full replay + remediation cycle.
- Week 3: Canary + ramp to production.
- Week 4: Post-cutover validation and close.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: Network characteristics (higher RTT) cause sustained latency regression.
  - Mitigation: Identify high-latency routes and recommend edge-local placement or TCP tuning; if not possible, schedule degraded SLO with customer consent.
- Risk: KV cache semantics differ in Private packaging causing cache miss spikes.
  - Mitigation: Run a targeted KV warmup stage before cutover and validate hit-rate progress.
- Risk: Underestimated GPU memory pressure after quantization differences.
  - Mitigation: Include memory-pressure stress tests in the replay and map to required instance types.

Appendix A — Useful commands and examples:
- Extract traces (CLI): redwood-audit export-traces --tenant $TENANT --days 7 --out ./traces.tar.gz
- Provision test cluster (example): redwood-cli private create-cluster --manifest migration-manifest.json --size small --tag migration-test
- Replay traffic (example): redwood-replay orchestrate --input traces.tar.gz --preserve-affinity --duration 2h --out ./results.json

Appendix B — Comparator quick-check matrix (example ASCII table):
| Metric                     | Hosted baseline | Private test | Delta | Pass? |
|---------------------------|----------------|--------------|-------|-------|
| Route P50 (ms)            | 42             | 45           | +7%   | PASS  |
| Route P90 (ms)            | 120            | 160          | +33%  | FAIL  |
| Request success (%)       | 99.96          | 99.89        | -0.07 | PASS  |
| KV cache hit (%)          | 78             | 60           | -18pt | FAIL  |

Open decisions (for review):
- Thresholds for automatic rollback at canary stage: should we use absolute latency deltas or percentile-weighted deltas? (product / SRE decision required)
- Default ephemeral cluster sizing: small vs medium for first run — recommend starting with small and escalate based on utilization.

References and related docs:
- Private reference architectures and packaging: /confluence/eng-private-deployments/reference-architectures
- Hosted-to-dedicated transition playbook (operational context): /confluence/product-docs/product-overview/hosted-to-dedicated-transition-playbook-2026-06-30

Next steps:
- Incorporate reviewer feedback and instrument Auditor to produce migration-manifest.json in a canonical schema.
- Deliver a curated migration-harness repo and example manifests for three pilot customers by end of Q3 2026.
